This video explores the story of the PNS Ghazi submarine Pakistan sent from Karachi to the Bay of Bengal to hunt down INS Vikrant and crush India’s support to the Mukti Bahini in East Pakistan. But destiny had other plans. The Indian Navy secretly relocated Vikrant to a safe, hidden anchorage and launched a brilliant deception to mislead Ghazi. 
INS Rajput and other naval units transmitted false radio signals and traffic mimicking Vikrant’s movements, creating a perfect decoy. As Ghazi closed in on the fake contact near Visakhapatnam, INS Rajput dropped depth charges, triggering a massive underwater explosion that destroyed the submarine. That single blast beneath the Bay of Bengal didn’t just sink the submarine, it changed the course of the 1971 India-Pakistan War and paved the way for the birth of Bangladesh.
